newsitem.title: USA: Argentine people to feel recovery in '97 - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Argentine people to feel recovery in '97 - cenbank.

text.p: The Argentine economy is well on the path to recovery, and the country's citizens will feel the rebound within six months, Argentina's Central Bank President Pedro Pou said Friday.
"As numbers start accumulating in the same direction, people will start to feel that the situation is improving," Pou told Reuters. "People will realize the change by the first quarter of 1997.
The Argentine government has faced increased opposition to its policies as unemployment remained mired at 17.1 percent.

On Friday, Argentina's largest trade federation ended a 36-hour general strike to oppose the high unemployment, the Peronists' drive for fiscal austerity, cuts in worker benefits and new labour laws that benefit employers.
Pou said that, despite the protests, the government would stick to its economic reforms.
"I haven't seen the government back down in any significant position and I don't expect it to do so," Pou said.
